title: Add records-branch schemas, CAS writer and host-rules check
summary: Job 1 of records-history: add six record types (landing-intent, landing, intervention, checkpoint, legacy-exempt, import-manifest) with validation to athena-data. Add a compare-and-swap writer with bounded retry for the own-root branch athena/records (§8.2), and a read-only report on host branch rules. Audience: the maintainer and the verifier, who run cargo test. Nothing in the job pipeline uses the branch yet.

defaults_applied.how: All code, including tests, is Rust.
Every new module has passing tests, and cargo test and clippy are clean.
Criteria run the concurrent-writer, retry and no-rewrite scenarios, not only check that types exist.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Use the git CLI through the existing athena-git wrapper and existing crates; record the call if any dependency is added.
Only job 1 of the plan; the importer and the pipeline wiring stay out.
Append-only and the retry bound are enforced in code and tests, not prose.
Doc comments cite the design section for an outside reader.
Tests use synthetic data only, with no secrets and no personal data.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The writer goes in athena-git, which drives the git CLI and has no Athena dependencies. It takes opaque (path, bytes) files, so athena-data stays free of git. A thin typed layer may combine the two.

The host-rules check goes in athena-core beside gh.rs, as a read-only query through the existing runner and gh abstraction, with the API replies parsed in unit tests with fixtures. It exposes no CLI wiring into the pipeline.
The new 'intervention' record is distinct from the existing athena.intervention record. It is a user declaration about a main commit and gets its own schema tag and type name.

Compare-and-swap uses git update-ref with the expected old value, or a push with a lease option. Retry is bounded (default 5). On rejection the writer fetches, replays its new files on the new tip, and retries.
Each record is a separate file keyed by job and record id. The writer refuses to modify, delete or rename an existing path in the tree.
Landing commits take the PR head as an extra parent; the writer supports additional parents but job 3 uses them.
The records/ tree on main, the history check, gate and job pipeline are unchanged. No governance file changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a test starts two writers at once against one repository, and both records are present on athena/records afterward, each as its own path, with the branch history fast-forward only.

Run cargo test: a test makes the compare-and-swap reject the first update because the tip moved. The writer refetches, replays its files on the new tip, retries and succeeds. A test also shows that after the retry bound it returns a failure instead of looping.
Run cargo test: a test shows the writer refuses a write that would modify, delete or rename an existing record path on the branch. The branch tip is unchanged after the refusal.
Run cargo test: the branch athena/records is created as its own root, with no parent in common with main.

Run cargo test: each of the six new record types round-trips through serde with a schema tag, and validation rejects malformed examples. Examples are an empty required field, an unknown field, and a bad sha.

Run cargo test: the host-rules check run against fixture replies reports 'forbidden' versus 'allowed' for force-push and deletion on athena/records, and 'required' versus 'not required' for up-to-date branches on main. It also reports an unavailable host as unknown rather than passing. It issues only read requests, and a test asserts no write call is made.
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check, then cargo test for the whole workspace: all pass. The existing history check and the records/ tests are unchanged.
No existing code path in athena-core, athena-cli or athena-gate calls the new writer or reads athena/records. records/ on main has no diff.
Public items carry doc comments citing docs/design/records-history.md §8.2 and D111. Any new crate dependency is recorded with the buy-first reasoning.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new record types, the writer and the check.

out_of_scope: The importer (job 2), landing intent and reconcile (job 3), the pre-merge status (job 4), the attribution check (job 5), the incremental check (job 6), the cutover and the removal.
Changing any host setting, branch protection, or workflow under .github/workflows/.
Any change to records/ on main, the history check, or the job pipeline.
Wiring the host-rules check into a CLI command or CI, beyond a callable function.
departures: This is larger than a typical change: a new schema, a concurrent git writer with tests, and a host-rules check across three crates. I raise cost and time above the reference and lower the pass odds.
